name: How does a bump-out addition differ from a full room addition?

mainEntity.name: How does a bump-out addition differ from a full room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out addition expands an existing room by a few feet, whereas a standard room addition constructs an entirely new enclosed room from scratch. A major practical tradeoff is cost and structural scope. Standard full additions typically require extensive excavation, full perimeter concrete foundations, and dedicated heating and cooling systems. A bump-out often cantilevers over an existing foundation or rests on simple piers or minimal stem walls, avoiding substantial ground disturbance. While a full addition yields hundreds of square feet of new living area, a bump-out solves specific layout constraints—like fitting a bathtub or breakfast area—at a lower total investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out expands the footprint of an existing room by a few feet, while a full room addition builds an entirely new standalone room requiring extensive foundation and utility work.
